Business.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:15pt;text-align:justify"><span id="i11cc124d71d84e1d84e0b4c9bc18ac1e"></span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Overview</span></div><div style="text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:115%">DBV Technologies is a late-stage specialty biopharmaceutical company focused on changing the field of immunotherapy by developing a novel technology platform called Viaskin. Our therapeutic approach is based on epicutaneous immunotherapy, or EPIT, our proprietary method of delivering biologically active compounds to the immune system through intact skin using Viaskin, an epicutaneous patch (i.e., a skin patch). We have generated significant data demonstrating that Viaskin patch&#8217;s mechanism of action is novel and differentiated. Viaskin patch targets antigen-presenting immune cells in the skin, called Langerhans cells, that capture the antigen and migrate to the lymph nodes in order to activate the immune system without passage of the antigen into the bloodstream, minimizing systemic exposure in the body. We are advancing this unique technology to treat children suffering from food allergies for whom safety is paramount since the introduction of the offending allergen into their bloodstream can cause severe or life-threatening allergic reactions, such as anaphylactic shock. We believe Viaskin technology may offer convenient, non-invasive immunotherapy to patients.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our most advanced product candidate is </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;letter-spacing:-0.025em;line-height:120%">Viaskin&#174;</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Peanut Patch, which has been evaluated as a potential therapy for children with peanut allergy in twelve completed clinical trials, including five Phase&#160;2 trials and five completed Phase&#160;3 trials. </span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Company plans a BLA submission in the first half of 2026 for </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;letter-spacing:-0.025em;line-height:120%">Viaskin</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Peanut Patch as a potential treatment for children four to seven years old. The Company also has an ongoing Phase&#160;3 supplementary safety study of Viaskin Peanut patch in peanut-allergic toddlers ages one through three. Conditional on successful completion of this safety study, the Company plans a BLA submission in the second half of 2026 for children ages one to three.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Company has earlier-stage food allergy programs including Viaskin Milk and other autoimmune inflammatory diseases. </span></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:15pt;text-align:justify"><span id="if0a8bee810ed402e999de5811450667b"></span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Our Strategy</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our goal is to change the field of immunotherapy by developing and commercializing safe, effective, and convenient therapies for patients with food allergies and other immunological conditions. Key elements of our strategy are:</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;padding-left:9.92pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-9.92pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:7.12pt">pursue the continued development of Viaskin</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Aptos',sans-serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#174;</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Peanut Patch for toddlers and children with peanut allergy;</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;padding-left:9.92pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-9.92pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:7.12pt">seek regulatory approval for Viaskin</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Aptos',sans-serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#174;</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> Peanut Patch in the United States and the European Union;</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;padding-left:9.92pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-9.92pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:7.12pt">advance the clinical development of additional Viaskin</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Aptos',sans-serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#174;</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> product candidates in the United States and other major markets;</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;padding-left:9.92pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-9.92pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:7.12pt">build a broad immunotherapy product pipeline with our innovative Viaskin</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Aptos',sans-serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#174;</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> technology platform.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:15pt;text-align:justify"><span id="id3abe2d002494660911a7e8172147b94"></span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">The U.S. Commercial Opportunity </span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Company is developing launch plans, subject to FDA approval of our product candidate, that are focused on addressing the unmet needs of patients, their caregivers, physicians, and payers. It is estimated that there are approximately 670,000 children ages 1 to 7 years old in the U.S. with peanut allergy. The parents and caregivers for these children are largely part of the millennials demographic which comprises 7.2 million people born between the years of 1981 and 1996. We believe the majority of millennials turn to digital spaces for health information and advice. If VIASKIN Peanut Patch is approved, the Company plans to launch digital and social-media campaigns to activate these parents and caregivers by encouraging shared-decision making conversations with their child&#8217;s allergist. There are approximately 4,500 allergists in the U.S. and anticipate that a 50 to 70 person specialty sales force can deliver in-person promotional activities to 90% of those physicians. Market research suggests nearly 60% of peanut allergic children are cared for by allergists. In addition, there are approximately 60,000 pediatricians that we anticipate engaging through non-personal promotion. Finally, approximately 50 payers in the U.S. cover 85% of insured lives and that a team of 8 to 10 account managers can be deployed to build strong managed care access.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:15pt;text-align:justify"><span id="i0fa0cdab6e9c45bf85186d669054361c"></span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Peanut Allergy</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:8pt;text-align:justify"><span id="ie66619c457b54c829bcc9ce95fcc8a58"></span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Unmet Medical Need</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Peanut allergy is one of the most common food allergies globally with an overall prevalence across all age groups of approximately 1%, which increases up to 2% in the pediatric population. Based on a 2018 publication, an estimated 2.2% of the pediatric population in the United States, approximately 1.6&#160;million children, is allergic to peanuts. This reflects an increasing prevalence, as has been shown by several epidemiologic studies, including a cross-sectional survey-based study in the United States in which the prevalence of peanut allergy more than tripled between 1997 and 2008 from 0.4% to 1.4%. Studies indicate that most children do not outgrow their peanut allergy, with resolution occurring in only about 20% of young children, making this allergy a life-long affliction in most cases.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Clinically, an allergic reaction to peanut is characterized by rapid onset of symptoms which are triggered by the release of mediators from mast cells and basophils and typically involves one or more target organs. Presentation and severity of allergic reactions are unpredictable and may vary from mild to severe (anaphylaxis) within populations and within individuals over time. In the case of peanut allergy, all individuals are considered at risk for severe allergic reactions, irrespective of their past history.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:8pt;margin-top:12pt;text-align:justify"><span id="i51924dc8b35143d0808118ea3d31b9f6"></span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Current Challenges in the Management of Peanut Allergy Patients</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The standard of care for the management of peanut allergy is strict allergen avoidance and the use of epinephrine in case of an allergic reaction. However, since peanut is a common ingredient in many foods, complete avoidance is difficult to achieve, and accidental exposures in peanut-allergic children remains a common issue. The estimated rate of accidental peanut exposure in peanut-allergic children is estimated to be 12.4% per year, with </span></div><div style="height:45.36pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:right"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:139%">F - 6</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"/><div style="min-height:45.36pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">approximately 40% of children experiencing an accidental exposure within three years of diagnosis. In addition, the constant vigilance required to avoid allergen exposure can affect the quality of life of peanut-allergic children and their parents/caregivers. Daily family activities and social events are negatively impacted by the anxiety and fear of accidental peanut ingestion. According to a 2020 publication, a survey conducted across eight European countries reported high rates of frustration, stress and isolation in peanut-allergic individuals and their caregivers. The current management of peanut allergy has significant limitations and highlights the need for safe and effective treatments that can induce clinical desensitization (i.e., increased tolerance to peanut allergen), thus minimizing the risk of reaction due to accidental ingestion.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:8pt;margin-top:12pt;text-align:justify"><span id="i643cd739396a4beebf1799cfa8d204ce"></span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Current and Emerging Peanut Allergy Treatments</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Several non-specific and allergen-specific treatment approaches are in various stages of clinical development for the treatment of peanut allergy. Food allergen-specific approaches include EPIT, oral immunotherapy (&#8220;OIT&#8221;), (both with and without adjunctive therapies), and sublingual immunotherapy (&#8220;SLIT&#8221;). EPIT is an emerging therapeutic approach to food allergy that utilizes the unique immune properties of the skin to deliver allergen directly to antigen-presenting cells in the epidermis and dermis to induce desensitization. Although efficacious, peanut OIT may not be suitable or a preferred option for all children with peanut allergy because of its relatively high rate of systemic side effects and the limitations the treatment places on activities of daily living, including exercise, and unpredictability of tolerance in the setting of intercurrent illness. A proprietary form of OIT, Palforzia&#174;, is approved in the US and the European Union for the treatment of peanut allergy in children aged 1&#8211;17&#160;years. In December 2025, Stallergenes Greer, which currently commercializes Palforzia, announced that the product will be discontinued on July 31, 2026, for business reasons. In February 2024, Xolair&#174; (omalizumab), an anti-immunoglobulin E (&#8220;IgE&#8221;) antibody, was approved by the FDA for the reduction of allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis, that may occur with accidental exposure to one or more foods in adult and pediatric patients aged 1&#160;year and older with IgE-mediated food allergy. SLIT for peanut allergy has demonstrated evidence of clinical success, with a more satisfactory side effect profile compared to OIT. Despite the evident interest of clinicians to further evaluate these treatment procedures, OIT and SLIT may not be applicable across all ages and risk categories of peanut-allergic children and adults.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Following its acquisition of RAPT Therapeutics in March 2026, GlaxoSmithKline (&#8220;GSK&#8221;) is developing ozureprubart, an IgE&#8209;pathway inhibitor with potential relevance for food&#8209;allergy treatment. With a Phase IIb readout expected in 2027 and Phase 3 trials planned thereafter, ozureprubart could emerge as a competitor in segments characterized by persistent unmet needs. </span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">There remains an unmet need for additional therapies for patients with a peanut allergy. In most other therapeutic areas, healthcare providers, patients, and their families have several treatment options, and they are able to choose the treatment that best fits their needs.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:15pt;text-align:justify"><span id="i03358cd7adff4af482b7591c85003560"></span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Our Viaskin Technology Platform</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Over the last few decades, we have developed an innovative immunotherapy technology platform, with the potential for sustained therapeutic effect, by delivering biologically active compounds, including antigens, via intact skin. Epicutaneous, also known as on the skin, immunotherapy, or EPIT, exposes tolerance-promoting immune cells in the skin to an adhesive patch containing a small (micrograms) dose of antigen, such as food protein. This technology platform, called Viaskin, is an innovative approach to potentially treating immunological disorders, with a primary focus on food allergy. In EPIT, intact skin is exposed to allergen via the Viaskin technology using a patch that contains microgram amounts of food protein. Allergen applied via EPIT is captured in the superficial layers of the skin by specialized antigen-presenting cells (Langerhans cells within the epidermis), as well as dermal dendritic cells, thus limiting exposure to the bloodstream. In experimental models, EPIT induced a population of regulatory T cells (&#8220;Tregs&#8221;) with specific properties that resulted in suppression of allergic symptoms and protection against further sensitizations. EPIT-induced epigenetic modifications favored a Treg-mediated immune response and a down regulated Th2 response and may play a role in the sustainability of effect. Based on our trials and research, we believe that EPIT has the potential to provide the intended benefits of a disease-modifying treatment in allergy, while avoiding severe or life-threatening allergic reactions.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The key elements of the Viaskin patch mechanism of action, illustrated below, are the following:</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;padding-left:9.92pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-9.92pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:7.12pt">Containing a dry layer of allergen in its center, the patch is positioned on intact skin, without prior preparation.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;padding-left:9.92pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-9.92pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:7.12pt">The occlusion chamber formed between the skin and the center of the patch promotes an accumulation of water.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;padding-left:9.92pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-9.92pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226;</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:7.12pt">The accumulation of water solubilizes the allergen and allows its passage into the epidermis.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:8.08pt"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:8.08pt"><img src="dbvt-20251231_g1.jpg" alt="DBV_DEU_2024_CH01_SchemaViaskin_FR.jpg" style="height:162px;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:682px" id="i-1"/></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span><br/></span></div><div style="height:45.36pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:right"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:139%">F - 7</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"/><div style="min-height:45.36pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Once in the epidermis, the allergen is captured by a population of highly specialized cells: Langerhans cells. These cells can capture the allergen at the surface of the skin, process it and migrate to the local lymph nodes to present allergen fragments to T-lymphocytes.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:center"><img src="dbvt-20251231_g2.jpg" alt="Visuel_2.jpg" style="height:156px;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:276px" id="i-2"/></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Langerhans cells in the epidermis capturing peanut allergen (depicted in green) within the stratum corneum (the outermost layer of the skin) following solubilization of allergen and permeation into the skin after Viaskin patch application.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:10pt;margin-top:15pt;text-align:justify"><span id="i49072e8668cf4366b9b97d4b8820667b"></span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Our Product Candidates</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our product development strategy is based on leveraging Viaskin&#8217;s clinical potential. </span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Our lead product style="height:45.36pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:right"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:139%">F - 8</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"/><div style="min-height:45.36pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:8pt;margin-top:12pt;text-align:justify"><span id="i9bf2bca74fce4ff9b57c519767420083"></span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Viaskin Peanut for Children ages 1-3</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We are developing Viaskin Peanut for the treatment of peanut allergy in toddlers one to three years of age, given the high unmet need and the limited number of approved treatments for this population. This program is independent from the Viaskin Peanut Program in 4-7-year-olds and uses the cVP (original patch).</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Viaskin Peanut program for toddlers comprises three Phase 3 clinical trials, with the intent for the trials to support a future BLA submission in this age group:</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226; EPITOPE (EPIT in Toddlers with Peanut Allergy), a randomized, two-part, pivotal Phase 3 clinical trial assessing the safety and efficacy of Viaskin Peanut for the treatment of peanut-allergic toddlers one to three years of age;</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226; COMFORT Toddlers (Characterization of the Optimal Management of Food allergy Relief and Treatment), a supplemental safety study to bring the (total) number of subjects on active therapy close to 600 in total when combined with EPITOPE;</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226; EPOPEX (Phase 3 Open-Label Extension to the EPITOPE Trial), a follow-up of the EPITOPE study to evaluate the long-term efficacy and safety of Viaskin Peanut in very young children.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In June 2022, we announced positive topline results from EPITOPE, which enrolled 362 subjects ages 1 to 3 years, of which 244 and 118 were in the active and placebo arms, respectively. Enrollment was balanced for age and baseline disease characteristics between the active and placebo treatment arms. The median subject baseline eliciting dose (&#8220;ED&#8221;) was 100 mg in each treatment arm. A double-blind, placebo-controlled food challenge (&#8220;DBPCFC&#8221;) was administered at baseline and month 12 to determine a subject&#8217;s ED at each timepoint. A treatment responder was defined as either a subject with a baseline ED &#8804;10 mg who reached an ED &#8805;300 mg of peanut protein at month 12, or a subject with a baseline ED &gt;10 mg and &#8804;300 mg who reached an ED &#8805;1,000 mg of peanut protein at month 12.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Viaskin Peanut demonstrated a statistically significant treatment effect (p&lt;0.001), with 67.0% of subjects in the Viaskin Peanut arm meeting the treatment responder criteria after 12 months, as compared to 33.5% of subjects in the placebo arm (difference in response rates = 33.4%; 95% the lower bound of the 95% confidence interval (&#8220;CI&#8221;) for the difference in response rates between the active and placebo groups was 22.4%, exceeding the predefined threshold of 15%); left hand side chart. In addition, the proportion of subjects achieving an ED of &#8805;1000 mg (equivalent to approximately three peanuts) after one year of treatment with Viaskin Peanut 250 &#956;g (&#8220;VP250&#8221;) was significantly increased relative to placebo (64.2% versus 29.6%; p&lt;0.001, right hand side chart).</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><table style="border-collapse:collapse;display:inline-table;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:97.485%"><tr><td style="width:1.0%"/><td style="width:48.900%"/><td style="width:0.1%"/><td style="width:1.0%"/><td style="width:48.900%"/><td style="width:0.1%"/></tr><tr><td colspan="3" style="padding:2px 1pt;text-align:left;vertical-align:top"><div><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">ED &#8805;&#160;1,000&#160;mg</span></div></td><td colspan="3" style="padding:2px 1pt;text-align:left;vertical-align:top"><div><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Treatment Responders </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:5.2pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;position:relative;top:-2.8pt;vertical-align:baseline">&#10013;</span></div></td></tr><tr style="height:153pt"><td colspan="3" style="padding:0 1pt;vertical-align:top"><div><img src="dbvt-20251231_g9.gif" alt="DBV_DEU_2025_CH01_ED-1000mg_FR.gif" style="height:191px;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:321px" id="i-13"/></div></td><td colspan="3" style="padding:0 1pt;vertical-align:top"><div><img src="dbvt-20251231_g10.gif" alt="DBV_DEU_2025_CH01_TreatmentResponders_FR.gif" style="height:191px;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:321px" id="i-14"/></div></td></tr></table></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8224;  Responder definition = If eliciting dose (ED) &#8804;10 mg at baseline, a subject is deemed a responder if ED &#8805;300 mg at M12. Alternatively, if ED &gt;10 mg and &lt;300 mg at baseline, a subject was deemed a responder if ED &#8805;1000 mg at M12.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The EPITOPE safety results were generally consistent with the safety profile of Viaskin Peanut 250 &#956;g observed in children with peanut allergy ages 4 years and older in prior clinical trials. No imbalance in the overall adverse event (&#8220;AE&#8221;) rate was observed in the trial between the active and placebo arms.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Overall, 21 subjects (8.6%) in the Viaskin Peanut arm and three subjects (2.5%) in the placebo arm experienced a serious adverse event (&#8220;SAE&#8221;). Only one of the SAEs (0.4%), which was mild periorbital edema (swelling around the eye) in the Viaskin Peanut arm, was deemed related to treatment. The most commonly reported adverse events were skin reactions localized to the administration site, the majority of which were mild to moderate in nature.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Fifty-five subjects (22.5%) in the Viaskin Peanut arm experienced an application site reaction that was assessed as severe by an investigator compared with 10 subjects (8.5%) in the placebo arm. Based on investigators&#8217; reported observations from examinations of the skin at each study visit, using the skin grading systems defined in the protocol, the severity of administration site skin reactions following patch application decreased throughout the course of the 12-month treatment period. Four (1.6%) subjects in the Viaskin Peanut arm experienced an anaphylactic reaction determined to be related to, or possibly related to, treatment. Among these anaphylactic reactions, three resolved with a single dose of epinephrine and one resolved without epinephrine. All anaphylactic reactions were mild to moderate in severity and were characterized mainly by skin and respiratory symptoms.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Eight subjects (3.3%) in the Viaskin Peanut arm discontinued due to adverse events. In the 12-month treatment period, the trial completion rate was 84.8% and was balanced between the Viaskin Peanut and placebo arms. Mean subject compliance to daily patch treatment was above 95% in both the active and placebo arms.</span></div><div style="height:45.36pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:right"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:139%">F - 9</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"/><div style="min-height:45.36pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">On May 10, 2023, the New England Journal of Medicine (&#8220;NEJM&#8221;) published results from the EPITOPE phase 3 clinical study that demonstrated EPIT with Viaskin Peanut was statistically superior to placebo in desensitizing children to peanut exposure by increasing the peanut dose that triggers allergic symptoms. As stated in an accompanying editorial piece, these data are seen as &#8220;very good news&#8221; for toddlers with peanut allergy, as there are currently no approved treatment options for peanut-allergic children under the age of 4 years.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:10pt;text-align:justify"><span id="ic0d339142f664feda6ea129139b8da9f"></span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Results from Open-label Extension to EPITOPE Study (EPOPEX)</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Following the 12-month treatment period of EPITOPE, eligible subjects could opt to enroll in the open-label, extension (&#8220;OLE&#8221;) study for up to three years of active total treatment. This ongoing, OLE to EPITOPE is known as EPOPEX and is evaluating the long-term clinical benefit of Viaskin Peanut in subjects who completed the Phase 3 EPITOPE trial. Subjects randomized to active treatment in EPITOPE could receive an additional two-years of treatment in the OLE and subjects randomized to placebo in EPITOPE cross-over to receive three years of active treatment with annual DBPCFC and safety assessments. 266 eligible EPITOPE participants enrolled in EPOPEX.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><img src="dbvt-20251231_g11.gif" alt="DBV_DEU_2025_CH01_EpitodeEpopex_FR.gif" style="height:285px;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:650px" id="i-15"/></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">244 underwent the month-24 DBPCFC (n=166 subjects treated with Viaskin Peanut 250 &#956;g for 24 months); 78 subjects originally randomized to the placebo arm of EPITOPE who crossed-over and received active treatment with Viaskin Peanut for one year in the OLE. In November 2023, we announced the interim analyses from the first year of the open-label extension of EPITOPE. These data were presented at the annual American College of Allergy, Asthma, and Immunology (&#8220;ACAAI&#8221;) in November 2023. Using the same primary endpoint definition that was used in EPITOPE, 83.9% of subjects who completed the DBPCFC met the responder criteria after 24 months. This compares to 67% of subjects after one year of therapy. 81.3% of Viaskin Peanut subjects reached an ED of &#8805;1000 mg (equivalent to approximately three peanuts; central chart), relative to 64% after one-year of treatment observed in EPITOPE. Furthermore, following an additional year of treatment, 55.9% completed the food challenge without meeting the stopping criteria (i.e., consumed the equivalent of about 12-14 peanuts).</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><table style="border-collapse:collapse;display:inline-table;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:97.485%"><tr><td style="width:1.0%"/><td style="width:32.233%"/><td style="width:0.1%"/><td style="width:1.0%"/><td style="width:32.233%"/><td style="width:0.1%"/><td style="width:1.0%"/><td style="width:32.234%"/><td style="width:0.1%"/></tr><tr><td colspan="3" style="padding:2px 1pt;text-align:left;vertical-align:bottom"><div><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">Treatment Responders </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:5.2pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%;position:relative;top:-2.8pt;vertical-align:baseline">&#10013;</span></div></td><td colspan="3" style="padding:2px 1pt;text-align:left;vertical-align:bottom"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">*ED &#8805; Local application site reactions continued to be the most reported adverse event, with frequency decreasing during the second year of treatment. The frequency of treatment related treatment-emergent advese events (&#8220;TEAEs&#8221;) also decreased in Year 2 relative to Year 1. There were no treatment related serious TEAEs reported during the second year of treatment (versus 1% in EPITOPE). As observed during the first year of treatment with Viaskin Peanut, no TEAEs led to permanent study treatment discontinuation. Finally, no treatment-related anaphylactic events were observed in the second year of treatment (compared with 1.7% of participants during the first year of treatment with Viaskin Peanut in EPITOPE). In summary, two years of VP250 in 1-3-year-old peanut-allergic toddlers resulted in continued increases in treatment effect, beyond those observed after one year, without any new safety signals.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In placebo-treated EPITOPE participants, outcomes after 12 months of cross-over to Viaskin Peanut in EPOPEX were consistent with EPITOPE treatment results: 68.0% were responders (compared to 67% of subjects on active treatment in the first year of EPITOPE); 62.7% of subjects reached an ED &#8805;1000 mg (relative to 64.2% in EPITOPE); 36.5% reached an ED &#8805;2000 mg (relative to 37% in EPITOPE); 28.4% completed the DBPCFC without meeting stopping criteria (relative to 30.7% in EPITOPE). After three years of VP250, 83.5% of participants reached an ED of &#8805;1000 mg, an increase from 64.2% at month 12 (the EPITOPE study). A similar increase was observed for participants reaching an ED of &#8805;2000 mg (72.7% at month 36; 37.0% at month 12). Those completing the DBPCFC without meeting stopping criteria increased to 68.2% at month 36 from 30.7% at month 12. Continued reductions in DBPCFC reaction severity occurred, with 66.5% having no/mild symptoms at month 36 vs 40.2% at month 12. No treatment-related anaphylaxis or serious treatment-related TEAEs occurred in Year 3. Local application-site reactions occurred less frequently in Year 3 vs Years 1 and 2. In placebo-treated EPITOPE participants, outcomes after 24 months of VP250 in the OLE were consistent with 24-month results in EPITOPE VP250 participants.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:10pt;text-align:justify"><span id="i3dc0aba69c8d4a9a99a86336f14485c5"></span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Supplemental Safety Study in Toddlers (COMFORT Toddlers)</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In April 2023, we received pre-BLA Type B Meeting Written Responses from the FDA related to the Viaskin Peanut program in toddlers. The FDA did not request an additional efficacy study in 1-3-year-olds (i.e., the Agency agreed that the primary endpoint was satisfactorily met in DBV&#8217;s Phase 3 trial EPITOPE). There was agreement with the FDA to conduct a supplemental safety study using the original square (&#8220;cVP&#8221;) Viaskin Peanut patch to augment the safety data collected from EPITOPE and have close to 600 total subjects on active treatment in the controlled safety database (&#8220;COMFORT Toddlers&#8221;).</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">On November 9, 2023, the Company submitted the protocol for its COMFORT Toddlers supplemental safety study in 1 &#8211; 3 years-old  to  FDA. The Company received comments and queries to the protocol from the FDA on March 11, 2024.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">On October 22, 2024, the Company announced positive regulatory updates for the Viaskin Peanut patch in the United States and Europe. DBV has agreed to guidance provided by the FDA on a potential pathway under the Accelerated Approval Program for the Viaskin Peanut patch in toddlers ages 1 &#8211; 3 years-old. FDA confirmed that the Company has met Accelerated Approval qualifying criteria 1 and 2. Regarding criterion 3, FDA has provided guidance and suggestion regarding the intermediate clinical endpoint, which the Company has agreed to in informal discussions with the FDA. The Company formalized the Accelerated Approval guidance provided by FDA via submission of a meeting request and confirmed the general elements of the two study components: the COMFORT Toddlers safety study, to be completed before BLA submission, and the confirmatory effectiveness study, including the third Accelerated Approval criterion regarding the intermediate clinical endpoint. The Company expects that the confirmatory study will be initiated by the time of BLA submission and would run in parallel to commercialization in the United States, if the Viaskin Peanut patch is approved.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span><br/></span></div><div style="text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">The Company announced further that it has aligned with FDA on a wear time collection methodology in COMFORT Toddlers that provides a practical approach for subjects and families, is intended to generate sufficient data to support a BLA submission, and places wear time into an acceptable clinical hierarchy relative to other study endpoints. On June 25, 2025, the Company announced that the first subject was screened in COMFORT Toddlers supplemental safety study in peanut allergic toddlers 1 &#8211; 3 years old. The Company anticipates enrolling approximately 300 &#8211; 350 subjects on active treatment into the COMFORT Toddlers safety study, which would bring the total Viaskin Peanut patch safety database in toddlers to approximately 600 subjects, consistent with prior FDA guidance.  With this path forward, the BLA submission for Viaskin Peanut patch in 1 &#8211; 3 years-old under the Accelerated Approval program is anticipated to be supported by:</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">i.               Positive efficacy and safety data from DBV&#8217;s previously completed EPITOPE Phase 3 Study; and</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">ii. &#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Additional safety data generated in COMFORT Toddlers supplemental safety study to be initiated in the second quarter of 2025.</span></div><div style="text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">On December 11, 2024, the Company announced that it reached alignment with FDA on the Accelerated Approval pathway for Viaskin Peanut patch in toddlers 1-3 years-old and on key study design elements for the COMFORT Toddlers study, including study size and wear time collection methodology and analysis.  The Company announced further that FDA confirmed criteria for a post-marketing confirmatory study in toddlers 1-3 years-old and that the Company and FDA agreed that the confirmatory study will assess the effectiveness of the intended commercial Viaskin Peanut patch and will need to be initiated at the time that the BLA is submitted.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:8pt;margin-top:12pt;text-align:justify"><span><br/></span></div><div style="height:45.36pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:right"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:139%">F - 11</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"/><div style="min-height:45.36pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:8pt;margin-top:12pt;text-align:justify"><span id="i00b02aa64a79472bb8c3f983c6fd97e6"></span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Viaskin Peanut for Children ages 4-7</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We are evaluating the modified (circular) Viaskin Peanut patch in children ages 4-7 years with peanut allergy in two Phase 3 clinical trials with the intent for the trials to support a future BLA submission in this age group.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:10pt;text-align:justify"><span id="ib8e8c50047694e4ea2bbe512ccd89980"></span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">VITESSE (Viaskin Peanut Immunotherapy Trial to Evaluate Safety, Simplicity and Efficacy)</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">On September 7, 2022, we announced the initiation of VITESSE, a new Phase 3 pivotal study of the modified Viaskin Peanut (&#8220;mVP&#8221;) patch in children ages 4-7 years with peanut allergy. We defined initiation as the submission of the trial protocol to selected study sites for subsequent Institutional Review Board (&#8220;IRB&#8221;) approval and Ethics Committee (EC) opinion.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">On September 21, 2022, the Company announced it received from the FDA a partial clinical hold letter related to certain design elements of VITESSE. The Company announced on December 23, 2022 that the FDA lifted the partial clinical hold. The FDA confirmed the Company satisfactorily addressed all clinical hold issues and the VITESSE phase 3 clinical study could proceed with the revised trial protocol. On March 7, 2023, the Company announced that the first patient was screened in the VITESSE trial. The Company announced on September 23, 2024 that subject screening has been completed in the third quarter of 2024.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;margin-top:10pt;text-align:justify"><img src="dbvt-20251231_g15.gif" alt="DBV_DEU_2025_CH01_GlobalPhase_FR.gif" style="height:338px;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:650px" id="i-19"/></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">We enrolled a total of 654 subjects for participation in the VITESSE study, randomized 2:1 active to placebo. The primary efficacy endpoint is the percentage of treatment responders in the active versus placebo arms at month 12. The primary efficacy analysis was the success criterion of the lower bound of the confidence interval of the difference in responder rates between active and placebo groups being greater than or equal to 15%.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">A treatment responder is defined as either a subject with a baseline ED &#8804;30 mg who reaches an ED &#8805;300 mg of peanut protein at month 12, or a subject with a baseline ED = 100 mg who reaches an ED &#8805;600 mg of peanut protein at month 12. A DBPCFC will be administered at baseline and month 12 to determine a subject&#8217;s ED at both timepoints. We defined the peanut protein sensitivity inclusion criteria to align with peanut allergy patients at the greatest risk of experiencing reactions to accidental peanut ingestion and with the highest unmet need. We added a 600 mg dose of peanut protein to the month 12 DBPCFC to increase the sensitivity of the efficacy assessment.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Participants applied the modified patch (either Viaskin Peanut 250 &#956;g or a placebo) daily for a period of 12 months. The maximum study duration per subject was 58 weeks: a four-week screening period, a 12-month treatment period and a two-week follow-up period. During the screening period, subjects  underwent an initial screening visit with assessment for eligibility according to peanut skin prick test (&#8220;SPT&#8221;) and serum peanut IgE.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Those meeting these criteria proceeded to a peanut DBPCFC to confirm their peanut allergy and establish an entry peanut ED. The entry DBPCFC was 1 mg peanut protein, and was escalated up to a highest single dose of 100 mg peanut protein. Subjects who reacted with an ED at or below the dose of 100 mg peanut protein were considered eligible. At month 12, a post-treatment DBPCFC was performed, with a starting dose of 3 mg peanut protein, escalating to a highest dose of 1,000 mg peanut protein according to the following schedule: 3, 10, 30, 100, 300, 600, 1,000 mg. Secondary efficacy endpoints included changes in Cumulative Reactive Dose, ED and severity of allergic reaction at baseline and month 12 food challenge. VITESSE  also evaluated the safety of the modified Viaskin Peanut patch based on overall adverse events, local site reactions and systemic allergic reactions.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The VITESSE Instructions for Use (&#8220;IFU&#8221;) directed caregivers to apply one patch at approximately the same time each day, following removal of the previous day&#8217;s patch. The updated IFU outlines that Viaskin Peanut 250 &#956;g is to be worn for as close to a full day as possible (i.e., 24 hours) with a minimum daily wear time of 20 hours each day.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Patch adhesion was assessed in VITESSE to affirm the modified Viaskin Peanut patch performs adequately, which aligns with existing regulatory requirements for patch-based therapies. In post-PCH discussions, we agreed with the FDA that a statistical test of adhesion would be included in the VITESSE statistical analysis plan and further considered patch adhesion data collection and interpretation in the context of the novel nature of the Viaskin patch platform.</span></div><div style="height:45.36pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:right"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:139%">F - 12</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"/><div style="min-height:45.36pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">On December 16, 2025, the Company announced the positive topline results from the VITESSE study and that its primary endpoint was met.  In VITESSE, Viaskin Peanut patch demonstrated a statistically significant treatment effect (p&lt;0.001), with 46.6% of children in the Viaskin Peanut patch arm meeting the treatment responder criteria after 12 months, as compared to 14.8% of children in the placebo arm (difference in response rates = 31.8%; 95% CI = (24.5, 39.0%)), exceeding the lower bound prespecified threshold of 15%. Safety results were consistent with the safety profile of the Viaskin Peanut clinical program to date. The most common TEAEs observed during the VITESSE study were mild-to-moderate local skin reactions at the patch application site. Discontinuations due to TEAEs were low at 3.2% in the treatment arm compared to 0.5% of in the placebo arm. Notably, there were no reports of treatment-related serious adverse events and treatment-related anaphylaxis was low at 0.5% (n=2) and both children continued treatment. The data from the exploratory adhesion assessments were in line with the Company&#8217;s expectations. Overall, compliance was high at 96.2%, consistent with what has been observed in other Phase 3 Viaskin Peanut studies. The Company is currently conducting the open-label extension phase of the VITESSE study. Following the 12-month double-blind period, participants were given the option to continue into an open-label extension of VITESSE in which all participants receive Viaskin Peanut patch for up to a total of three years on treatment.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">VITESSE Primary Endpoint&#160;: Percentage of Treatment Responders at M12 (ITT)</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><img src="dbvt-20251231_g16.gif" alt="DBV_DEU_2025_CH01_VITESSEPrimaryEndpoint_FR.gif" style="height:188px;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:302px" id="i-20"/></div><div style="margin-bottom:8pt;margin-top:12pt"><span id="ia93391fb28a04126a8614463c27d03ba"></span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:11pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Viaskin Peanut for children ages 4-11</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Viaskin Peanut completed a global Phase 3 development program for the treatment of peanut allergic patients four to 11 years of age. The program comprised of the following clinical trials:</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226; PEPITES (Peanut EPIT Efficacy and Safety Study), a randomized, placebo-controlled pivotal Phase 3 trial investigating the safety and efficacy of Viaskin Peanut 250 &#956;g in 356 patients after 12 months of treatment.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226; REALISE (REAL Life Use and Safety of EPIT), a randomized, placebo-controlled Phase 3 trial designed to generate safety data after six months of blinded treatment, as well as to evaluate the use of Viaskin Peanut 250 &#956;g in routine clinical practice.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">&#8226; PEOPLE (PEPITES Open Label Extension Study), a long-term, open-label extension trial of Viaskin Peanut 250 &#956;g. In the PEOPLE trial, patients who were randomized and received active treatment during PEPITES received Viaskin Peanut 250 &#956;g for up to four additional years, while patients who received placebo during PEPITES were treated with Viaskin Peanut 250 &#956;g for up to five years.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The results from PEPITES and REALISE formed the basis for our 2019 regulatory submission in the United States, a  BLA for the use of Viaskin Peanut in peanut-allergic patients four to 11 years of age. The results from PEPITES, REALISE and PEOPLE formed the basis for our 2020 regulatory submission in the European Union, a Marketing Authorization Application (&#8220;MAA&#8221;) for the use of Viaskin Peanut in peanut-allergic patients four to 11 years of age.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:10pt;text-align:justify"><span id="i3014b27b467145fe9163b43d46ce81eb"></span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">PEPITES (Peanut EPIT Efficacy and Safety Study)</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In December&#160;2015, we initiated a pivotal Phase&#160;3 trial designed to evaluate the safety and efficacy of Viaskin Peanut 250&#160;&#956;g in children four to 11&#160;years of age suffering from peanut allergy. PEPITES was a global, randomized 2:1, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase&#160;3 trial, in which 356&#160;pediatric peanut-allergic patients were treated with Viaskin Peanut 250&#160;&#956;g or placebo for 12&#160;months. A new patch was applied each day, and after two weeks, each patch was worn for 24&#160;hours, plus-or-minus 4&#160;hours. During the trial, patients&#8217; sensitivity to peanut protein was assessed using a  DBPCFC at baseline and again after 12&#160;months of treatment. The DBPCFC was halted once the patient exhibited an objective symptom, as described on a pre-specified scale, thus establishing a subject&#8217;s peanut reactivity level, also known as the patient&#8217;s ED. The median baseline reactive dose in PEPITES was 100&#160;mg at baseline.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The primary responder analysis was conducted after 12&#160;months of treatment. For patients with a baseline peanut protein ED equal to or less than 10&#160;mg, a responder was defined as a patient with a peanut protein ED equal to or greater than 300&#160;mg of peanut protein after 12&#160;months of treatment. For patients with a baseline ED greater than 10&#160;mg but less than or equal to 300&#160;mg, a responder was defined as a patient with a peanut protein ED equal to or greater than 1,000&#160;mg of peanut protein after 12&#160;months of treatment. Secondary endpoints included the change from baseline of mean and median cumulative reactive dose (&#8220;CRD&#8221;) of peanut protein which is used to establish the total quantity of peanut protein consumed during the DBPCFC. Serological markers were also measured at baseline, three, six and 12&#160;months to characterize the immunological changes observed in patients.</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:6pt;margin-top:10pt;text-align:justify"><span id="iaefcef1276c948dea54b5df4f7108028"></span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:10pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Results of PEPITES Trial</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">In October 2017, we announced topline results from PEPITES, in which we observed a statistically significant response with a favorable tolerability profile, with (based on &#8220;responder&#8221; definitions above) 35.3% of patients responding to Viaskin Peanut 250&#160;&#956;g after 12&#160;months of treatment as compared to 13.6% of patients in the placebo arm (difference in response rates = 21.7%; p=0.00001; 95% CI = 12.4%&#8212;29.8%). However, the primary endpoint, which evaluated the 95% CI in the difference in response rates between the active and placebo arms, did not reach the 15% lower bound of the CI that was proposed in the study&#8217;s Statistical Analysis Plan submitted to the FDA. The clinical relevance of this is not known. Detailed results were published in </span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">The Journal of the American Medical Association</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%"> (JAMA) in February&#160;2019.</span></div><div style="height:45.36pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:right"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:139%">F - 13</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"/><div style="min-height:45.36pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div></div><div><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Response Rate (ITT) after 12&#160;months</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:center"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">With respect to CRD, a key secondary endpoint which measures threshold reactivity during the DBPCFC, we observed that at month&#160;12, patients treated with Viaskin Peanut 250&#160;&#956;g or placebo reached a mean CRD of 906&#160;mg (median 444&#160;mg) and 361&#160;mg (median 144&#160;mg) of peanut protein, respectively. Patients in the active and placebo arms entered the trial at similar sensitivity levels; mean CRD at baseline was 211.7&#160;mg (median 144&#160;mg) in the Viaskin Peanut arm and 212.5&#160;mg (median 144&#160;mg) in the placebo arm. A difference in the CRD was observed between Viaskin Peanut and placebo (nominal p-value &lt;0.001) following 12&#160;months of treatment.</span></div><div style="text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">Response Rate (ITT) after 12 Months</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;margin-top:10pt;text-align:justify"><img src="dbvt-20251231_g17.gif" alt="DBV_DEU_2025_CH01_ITT-apres12Mois_FR.gif" style="height:223px;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:374px" id="i-21"/></div><div><span><br/></span></div><div><span><br/></span></div><div><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">CRD after 12&#160;months</span></div><div><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><img src="dbvt-20251231_g18.gif" alt="DBV_DEU_2025_CH01_CRD-apres12Mois_FR.gif" style="height:264px;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:374px" id="i-22"/></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:justify"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Exploratory analyses showed that changes in peanut-specific biomarkers, including IgE, and immunoglobulin G4 (&#8220;IgG4&#8221;), support the immunomodulatory effect of Viaskin Peanut. The median observed increase from baseline in peanut-specific IgE was greater in the Viaskin Peanut group vs placebo group, respectively, at month&#160;3 (70.1&#160;kilounits of antibody per liter (&#8220;kUA/L&#8221;) vs. 9.8&#160;kUA/L) and month&#160;6 (27.4&#160;kUA/L vs. 1.32&#160;kUA/L). However, at month&#160;12, peanut-specific IgE levels were observed to return to near baseline in both groups (1.1&#160;kUA/L vs. -1.1&#160;kUA/L). Median peanut-specific IgG4 were observed to increase over time in the Viaskin Peanut group (change from baseline at month&#160;3: 0.81&#160;mg/L; month&#160;6: 1.79&#160;mg/L; month&#160;12: 3.27&#160;mg/L), while levels remained unchanged from baseline in the placebo group. The change from baseline in peanut-specific IgG4 was greater at all time points with Viaskin Peanut vs. placebo, and the groups were observed to be highly distinguished by this marker, given a flat trend in the placebo arm. These changes are consistent with trends that have been observed with other forms of immunotherapy such as for venom and inhalant allergies.</span></div><div style="height:45.36pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:4pt;text-align:right"><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:139%">F - 14</span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"/><div style="min-height:45.36pt;width:100%"><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div><div style="margin-bottom:4pt"><span><br/></span></div></div><div><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:9pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">PEPITES Immunological Responses</span></div><div><table style="border-collapse:collapse;display:inline-table;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:97.485%"><tr><td style="width:1.0%"/><td style="width:48.900%"/><td style="width:0.1%"/><td style="width:1.0%"/><td style="width:48.900%"/><td style="width:0.1%"/></tr><tr style="height:179pt"><td colspan="6" style="border-bottom:0.3pt solid #000000;padding:0 1pt;vertical-align:top"><div style="text-align:center"><img src="dbvt-20251231_g19.jpg" alt="Graph VP.jpg" style="height:224px;margin-bottom:5pt;vertical-align:text-bottom;width:658px" id="i-23"/></div></td></tr><tr><td colspan="6" style="border-top:0.3pt solid #000000;padding:2px 1pt;text-align:left;vertical-align:top"><div><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:100%">IQR</span><span style="color:#000000;font-family:'Times New Roman',serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:100%">=interquartile range&#160;;
